# Roy Gardner

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047)</sub>
- **Origin:** Kingsport  <sub>[v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047)</sub>
- **Role:** College student  <sub>[v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Roy  <sub>[v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047)</sub>

## Appearance

Roy is adorably handsome with glorious dark eyes. He features a dark, dreamy, inscrutable appearance complemented by a deep, black, velvety smile.

_Sources: [v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047), [v3 c25 P48](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0048), [v3 c26 P18](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0018), [v3 c27 P36](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0036)_

## Personality

Roy possesses unfailing and deferential courtesy, along with a delightful pleading voice. He is romantic and clever, though he lacks a sense of humor and cannot grasp jokes. Despite his dramatic and melancholy presence, his sister Dorothy describes him as a sweet boy who can ultimately be uninteresting.

_Sources: [v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047), [v3 c26 P18](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0018), [v3 c27 P36](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0036), [v3 c39 P2](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0002)_

## History

Roy Gardner was forced to interrupt his college education to accompany his ill mother abroad for two years. Upon returning to Redmond College in Kingsport, he began courting Anne Shirley, sending her white orchids and romantic sonnets. His polite manners gained him the strong favor of Aunt Jamesina and most residents of Patty's Place. Throughout their college years, he courted Anne steadily, writing her exquisite letters twice a week during breaks, leading everyone to anticipate their engagement. However, when he finally proposed to Anne near the sea, she realized she did not truly love him and refused his proposal.

_Sources: [v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047), [v3 c26 P1](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0001), [v3 c26 P18](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0018), [v3 c27 P36](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0036), [v3 c28 P22](../source/v03-c28.md#nw-v03-c28-p0022), [v3 c37 P31](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0031), [v3 c38 P29](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0029), [v3 c38 P35](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0035)_
